decisions.question: Who is the sole consenting runner, and which OAuth scope may the witness use?

admissible_options.benefit: Binds one accountable human runner and the minimum exact scope without publishing provider identity.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: The confirming owner-operator must personally operate the later OAuth flow; changing runners requires a new decision graph.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when the confirming activity-evidence privacy owner is also the consenting witness runner.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: The later external-effect envelope must bind a non-public digest of the resolved provider/principal identity and reject any different runner.

admissible_options.benefit: Avoids recording runner consent before the operator is ready.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: OWNER-BWSL-001 and SWU-BWSL-002 remain blocked.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when the privacy owner and witness runner are not yet the same confirmed person.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: No external-effect request may be prepared.

admissible_options.benefit: Ends the live-witness route with no private-data or provider effect.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: The synthetic implementation remains the terminal evidence; BLK-STRAVA-ACTIVITY-001 stays open.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when no live witness should be run.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: The sequence terminates before SWU-BWSL-002.

decisions.question: Which witness fields may persist in a non-private receipt?

admissible_options.benefit: Proves the witness and disposition while minimizing linkability and disclosure.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: Reviewers cannot see the activity name, timestamp, distance, duration, speed, payload digest, or eligible-activity count; they verify typed outcomes and contract identity instead.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when public reproducibility needs proof of behavior, not runner or activity details.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: The real-witness receipt validator must reject activity values, payload-derived digests, activity counts, and direct provider, principal, and activity identifiers.

admissible_options.benefit: Makes the redacted activity summary directly inspectable.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: Name and start-date values can increase linkability even without tokens or coordinates; publication is irreversible.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose only when direct public inspection outweighs the added privacy exposure.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: All eight values become permitted public evidence and cannot later be made undisclosed.

admissible_options.benefit: Prevents accidental publication while the field policy is unsettled.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: The real witness remains blocked.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when the privacy owner needs a separate receipt-design review.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: No witness receipt or external-effect request may be admitted.

admissible_options.benefit: Publishes no runner or activity evidence.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: No live compatibility evidence is produced.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when even minimal proof publication is unwanted.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: The sequence terminates before SWU-BWSL-002.

decisions.question: How long may the real activity-evidence row persist, and what happens at expiry?

admissible_options.benefit: Minimizes persistent private activity data and proves cleanup in the same controlled attempt.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: Investigation after the attempt relies on typed statuses because the row is gone; a same-process finally is insufficient, so an independent cleanup supervisor is a mandatory pre-effect dependency.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose for a one-off compatibility witness whose purpose does not require later activity inspection and whose operator can validate the supervisor first.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: Normal cleanup deletes the exact row in the same attempt with a 15-minute operating target. No crash-safe hard ceiling is claimed; the external-effect gate blocks unless an independent supervisor can perform the same cleanup after primary-process failure.

admissible_options.benefit: Allows a longer manual review window before deletion.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: No automatic expiry scheduler exists; privacy and operator-failure exposure are materially greater.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose only if manual inspection of the stored evidence is necessary and an operator owns the deadline.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: The gate must name a deletion operator and later disposition receipt before the witness can close.

admissible_options.benefit: Avoids creating evidence without an accepted expiry rule.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: The witness remains blocked.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when neither retention window is acceptable yet.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: No real evidence may be created.

admissible_options.benefit: Creates no retention obligation.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: No live witness is produced.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when real evidence should never be persisted.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: The sequence terminates before SWU-BWSL-002.

decisions.question: Which evidence copies and derived state must disposition remove?

admissible_options.benefit: Matches the implemented transaction and keeps the descendant inventory finite.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: The witness must abort if any backup, cache, or private-log copy is enabled or discovered.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose for an isolated witness environment with backups and caches disabled.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: Delete the exact witness evidence row, reset the SuggestedTrack only if it has no other candidates, verify no app-controlled copies of that row remain, retain the minimal non-private receipt, and explicitly report all identity, track, unrelated-evidence, and provider-side residue.

admissible_options.benefit: Prevents a witness in an environment whose copy inventory is uncertain.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: The witness remains blocked.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when backups, caches, or logs cannot yet be proven absent.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: No real evidence may be created.

admissible_options.benefit: Avoids deletion and descendant-copy risk entirely.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: No live witness is produced.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when an isolated no-copy environment is unavailable.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: The sequence terminates before SWU-BWSL-002.

decisions.question: What must consent revocation do, and which disposition proof is required?

admissible_options.benefit: Exercises the real deletion and provider-revocation paths and proves repeat safety.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: Runner profile and disconnected provider-account metadata intentionally persist; auth principal, grant, consumed-state, and durable-session disposition are not proved. Only the exact witness evidence row and provider tokens are deleted. The owner must explicitly accept that residue.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when actual cleanup evidence is required and the retained identity metadata is acceptable.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: Exact-row disposition must return disposed then already_absent; provider revocation must delete tokens, disconnect the account, and return disposed then already_absent; the public receipt records typed statuses and exact-row/token absence only.

admissible_options.benefit: Avoids accepting the current profile/account residue.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: A stricter erasure operation would need a separately authorized implementation unit.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when disconnected account metadata or runner-profile persistence is unacceptable.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: OWNER-BWSL-001 remains blocked pending a new implementation.

admissible_options.benefit: Creates no new consent-revocation obligation.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: No live witness is produced.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when the current deletion boundary should not be used with real data.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: The sequence terminates before SWU-BWSL-002.

decisions.question: How long may the external witness attempt run, and may it retry?

admissible_options.benefit: Minimizes credential and evidence exposure while preserving one complete bounded attempt.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: Any provider, token-refresh, cleanup-supervisor, or validation failure ends the attempt; retry requires a new exact graph and authorization.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when the operator can complete OAuth, the two declared page-1 activity fetches, one evidence submission, receipt capture, and supervised cleanup in 15 minutes.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: The later external-effect request must enumerate exact calls and fail closed without retry.

admissible_options.benefit: Provides more operator time without adding a retry.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: Credentials and evidence may exist for four times longer than the recommended window.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when the environment cannot reliably complete the same one attempt in 15 minutes.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: The later request uses a 60-minute hard ceiling but still forbids retry.

admissible_options.benefit: Avoids starting an inadequately bounded external attempt.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: The witness remains blocked.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when neither proposed window is operationally credible.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: No external-effect request may be admitted.

admissible_options.benefit: Makes no provider call.
admissible_options.cost_or_risk: No live witness is produced.
admissible_options.when_to_choose: Choose when no bounded external attempt should occur.
admissible_options.downstream_impact: The sequence terminates before SWU-BWSL-002.

runner_identity_and_scope.consenting_runner: the human activity-evidence privacy owner who sends the exact confirmation and later personally operates the OAuth flow
runner_identity_and_scope.private_runtime_binding: the later external-effect request must bind a non-public digest of the resolved Body War principal and provider identity; a mismatch stops before activity fetch

retention_and_expiry.normal_path_ends_at: verified cleanup in the same attempt
retention_and_expiry.pre_effect_requirement: an independently running cleanup supervisor must be validated against the exact witness identity and candidate locator before OAuth starts
retention_and_expiry.normal_failure_behavior: run exact evidence disposition and provider revocation in finally; report failure if either cleanup proof is incomplete
retention_and_expiry.abnormal_termination_behavior: the independent supervisor invokes the same exact cleanup operations; absent supervisor readiness blocks before OAuth
retention_and_expiry.terminal_pass_requirement: the exact witness row and provider tokens rehash absent and the cleanup supervisor returns terminal PASS
retention_and_expiry.retained_app_activity_evidence_after_ver: none for the exact witness row; unrelated candidates are untouched

delete: all Body War provider tokens for the consenting principal through provider-access revocation
deletion_scope.derived_state: reset the affected SuggestedTrack to needs_evidence only when no other evidence candidate remains
deletion_scope.abort_condition: any backup, cache, or private-log copy is enabled, discovered, or cannot be evaluated
persistent_residue: the SuggestedTrack row persists with status reset only when its final candidate is removed
auth principal, grants, consumed OAuth state, and durable session lifecycle are outside the current evidence-disposition proof
the source activity and provider-side request records persist at Strava
the permitted non-private witness receipt persists
deletion_scope.external_provider_source_activity: out of scope and not deleted from Strava

bounded_external_attempt.expected_behavior: one owner-operated OAuth flow, one page-1/per_page=12 provider listing for UI selection, one page-1/per_page=50 provider listing for evidence-POST revalidation, one eligible activity selection, one evidence submission, receipt capture, and supervised cleanup
known_app_owned_provider_calls: one OAuth token exchange POST after the owner-operated callback
bounded_external_attempt.token_refresh_behavior: the effect preflight must prove the newly issued token is unexpired before the first listing; expiry or refresh need stops before the normal seam, with no refresh or retry authorized
bounded_external_attempt.cleanup_supervisor: mandatory and independent of the primary witness process
bounded_external_attempt.failure_behavior: fail closed, invoke supervised cleanup, and require a new exact external-effect graph before any later attempt

standing_noncommittal_choice.label: Explain / more context
standing_noncommittal_choice.behavior: expand all six decisions with aligned examples, then present the same real options again

aggregate_acceptance_semantics.exact_confirmation_selects: all six recommended action options and attests that the confirmer is the consenting privacy owner-operator runner
aggregate_acceptance_semantics.exact_confirmation_does_not_select: any rejected or alternative admissible option
aggregate_acceptance_semantics.different_selection: requires explicit per-decision option IDs and a newly frozen decision graph

review_history.disposition: superseded by revision 2 before any owner request

post_selection_boundary.OWNER-BWSL-001: may become PASS only after exact confirmation is durably consumed and the accepted graph rehashes unchanged
post_selection_boundary.SWU-BWSL-002: remains blocked-external-effect until a separate immutable effect envelope is independently reviewed and exactly authorized

claim_ceiling: This graph is a no-effect privacy-policy proposal. It selects nothing before exact owner confirmation and can never by itself authorize credentials, private data, provider calls, real evidence mutation, publication, deployment, release, or production use.
